reviewFindings.title: Preserve the cancellation signal when draining queued requests
reviewFindings.body: The default `submit(input, { signal })` path stores the signal, but `drain()` reconstructs the task as `{ input: task.input }` before calling `execute`. If the caller aborts before draining, the worker sees no signal and invokes transport instead of rejecting; if cancellation happens after execution starts, transport likewise receives `signal: undefined`. Thus neither advertised cancellation mode works for queued requests. Pass the complete task through the drain adapter so the existing worker check and transport forwarding apply to both entrypoints.

result.solutionAssessment: No, the implementation is incomplete because the default entrypoint discards the new task field. Forwarding the complete task through the existing drain adapter is the narrow repair; no new cancellation owner or queue layer is needed.

reviewFindings.title: Preserve the cancellation signal when draining queued requests
reviewFindings.body: The new `signal` is stored on the queued task, but `drain()` still calls `execute({ input: task.input }, transport)`, discarding it. Consequently, `submit(input, { signal })` followed by abort and drain still invokes transport, and a queued request already running never receives the caller's signal either. Since queued execution is the default, the advertised cancellation support fails on the primary path. Pass the complete task through the drain adapter.

result.solutionAssessment: No, the implementation is incomplete: the shared worker is an appropriate owner, but queued execution must pass it the signal rather than reconstruct an input-only task.
